rationale: The committee needs a map of a scattered field (tasks, supervision, measures, outcomes and scope) rather than a pooled effect, which is the purpose of a scoping review. The retrieved records show accuracy data for admission histories (c1), a single discharge programme (c2), jurisdiction-bound scope (c3) and inconsistent outcome definitions (c4), all of which argue for charting rather than pooling. The JBI approach with PRISMA-ScR reporting fits the four-hour-a-week resource if screening is shared.
alternatives: Systematic review of accuracy (refused: the committee's question is broader than accuracy and outcomes are defined inconsistently)
Survey of nearby hospitals only (refused: would miss regulatory scope and published programmes)
Decide without a review (refused: the committee asked for the evidence)
whyNotMoreComplex: Pooling is not possible with inconsistent definitions; a map answers what the committee needs to decide by April.

decision.statement: Conduct a scoping review of pharmacy technicians' roles in medication reconciliation at care transitions, charting tasks, training and supervision, accuracy measures and definitions, reported outcomes and regulatory scope by jurisdiction and date, for the April 2027 committee, with dual screening by a second reviewer.
decision.question: Should the pharmacy department run a scoping review before the committee decides on technicians' discharge role?

criteria.text: The field is scattered across designs and jurisdictions with inconsistent outcome definitions, so a map is the useful product.
An up-to-date review answering the same questions is found during screening.

gates.requirement: Library database access and interlibrary loans for the reviewing pharmacist
gates.evidence: Library ticket LIB-2026-412 dated 2026-09-14, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Release of the pharmacy resident for 0.2 FTE from January 2027 as second reviewer for dual screening

alternatives: Single-reviewer screening with verification of a sample
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4 from the second, non-empty search. The second-reviewer gate stays unknown until the residency director replies.

summary: Scoping review recommended; the decision rests on four ledger claims and waits on the second-reviewer gate.
